name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
description: Discover Lady Liberty, explore immigration stories and enjoy harbor views. Take the official ferry to both islands; the museum exhibits bring generations of arrivals to life.
do: See the statue, visit Ellis Island, take photos, listen to the audio tour.
why: An unforgettable symbol of New York and an excellent chance to discuss history.
location: Liberty Island; ferry from The Battery, Lower Manhattan, south of Wall Street. Take subway 1 to South Ferry or 4/5 to Bowling Green.

name: Brooklyn Bridge
description: Walk across the East River on a famous suspension bridge with beautiful Manhattan skyline views. The pedestrian path is above the traffic.
do: Walk, take skyline photos, explore DUMBO afterwards.
why: Free, spectacular and ideal for practising directions.
location: Between City Hall in Lower Manhattan and DUMBO in Brooklyn; take 4/5/6 to Brooklyn Bridge–City Hall.

name: Grand Central Terminal
description: Admire the celestial ceiling and elegant architecture of this bustling railway terminal. Find the Whispering Gallery near the Oyster Bar.
do: Explore the main concourse, try the whispering trick, find the market.
why: A remarkable landmark with a surprising secret.
location: Midtown East at 42nd Street and Park Avenue; subway 4/5/6/7/S to Grand Central.

name: SUMMIT One Vanderbilt
description: Experience mirrored rooms, skyline panoramas and playful installations high above Midtown. The reflective surfaces make this different from an ordinary viewpoint.
do: Explore immersive art, take photos and admire the skyline.
why: An unusual combination of art and spectacular views.
location: Midtown East, beside Grand Central Terminal; subway to Grand Central–42 St.

name: Roosevelt Island Tramway
description: Ride a cable car above the East River to a quieter island with striking views of Manhattan and the Queensboro Bridge.
do: Ride the tram, stroll along the waterfront, visit Four Freedoms Park.
why: A surprising local experience rather than a standard sightseeing bus.
location: Tram station at East 59th Street and Second Avenue, Upper East Side; ride to Roosevelt Island.
price: Standard MTA fare; verify current fare

name: Staten Island Ferry
description: Enjoy a public ferry journey across New York Harbor with views of Lower Manhattan and the Statue of Liberty from a distance. It does not stop at Liberty Island.
do: See the harbor, photograph the skyline, practise asking for boarding directions.
location: Whitehall Terminal at the southern tip of Manhattan; subway 1 to South Ferry.

name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
description: Explore an enormous collection of paintings, sculptures and historical objects from across the world. Choose a few galleries instead of trying to see everything.
do: Ask about exhibitions, admire masterpieces, browse the museum shop.
why: World-class art in a magnificent building by Central Park.
location: Upper East Side, Fifth Avenue at 82nd Street, east of Central Park; subway 4/5/6 to 86 St, then walk west.
image_query: Metropolitan Museum of Art New York

name: Tenement Museum
description: Join a guided apartment or neighborhood tour that tells the stories of families who lived on the Lower East Side. The experience feels personal and conversational.
do: Ask your guide questions and discover everyday immigrant life.
why: A moving, unusual alternative to a traditional museum.
location: Lower East Side, Orchard Street, southeast Manhattan; subway F to Delancey St or J/M/Z to Essex St.
price: Guided tours $30 adult + possible $3 service fee

name: Museum of the Moving Image
description: Discover how films, television and video games are made through interactive displays and changing exhibitions.
do: Explore screen history, try interactive exhibits, discuss favorite films.
why: An original choice for curious visitors.
location: Astoria, Queens; subway R to Steinway St or N/W to 36 Ave, then walk.
price: Ticket prices vary; see official admissions

name: Little Island
description: Explore a landscaped park built on sculptural columns above the Hudson River. Paths lead to unexpected viewpoints and performance spaces.
do: Walk among gardens, relax and admire the river.
why: A creative waterfront park that feels unlike anywhere else.
location: Chelsea / Meatpacking District at Pier 55, west of the High Line; subway A/C/E/L to 14 St, walk west.
price: Generally free entry; some performances ticketed

name: The High Line
description: Follow a former railway track transformed into a green walkway above Manhattan streets, with art, plants and striking architecture.
do: Walk, photograph public art, stop at Chelsea Market.
why: A beautiful example of New York reinventing its spaces.
location: West Side, from Meatpacking District north toward Hudson Yards; subway A/C/E/L to 14 St.

name: Green-Wood Cemetery
description: Explore a peaceful historic landscape in Brooklyn with elaborate monuments, winding paths and skyline views. Check visitor rules and tours.
do: Walk respectfully, discover history and architecture.
why: A genuinely unexpected New York destination.
location: Greenwood Heights, Brooklyn, southwest of Prospect Park; subway R to 25 St.
price: Grounds generally free; guided tours extra

name: DUMBO & Brooklyn Bridge Park
description: Explore cobbled streets, creative shops and iconic views of Manhattan Bridge framed by brick buildings. The waterfront is especially atmospheric.
do: Take photos on Washington Street, browse shops, walk in the park.
why: One of Brooklyn’s most photogenic areas.
location: DUMBO, northwest Brooklyn; subway F to York St or A/C to High St.
price: Free to explore; shopping and food extra

name: Chelsea Market
description: Explore an indoor market filled with food vendors, specialty shops and interesting industrial architecture. Great for asking about ingredients and recommendations.
do: Taste something new, order lunch, browse boutiques.
why: A lively setting for practical English conversations.
location: Chelsea, 75 Ninth Avenue, just east of the High Line; subway A/C/E/L to 14 St.

name: Chinatown & Columbus Park
description: Wander busy streets with markets, bakeries and restaurants, then enjoy the atmosphere of Columbus Park. Be curious and respectful.
do: Explore shops, ask for food recommendations, order a snack.
why: An energetic neighborhood for real-world interaction.
location: Lower Manhattan, east of SoHo and north of the Civic Center; subway 6/N/Q/R/W/J/Z to Canal St.

name: Broadway Theater District
description: Choose a musical or play in the famous theater district. Compare showtimes, seat locations and ticket conditions before buying.
do: Ask about seats, book a show, enjoy an evening performance.
why: An iconic New York evening and a realistic booking challenge.
location: Midtown West around Times Square, west of Fifth Avenue; subway N/Q/R/W/1/2/3/7 to Times Sq–42 St.
price: Prices vary widely by show and date

name: Lincoln Center
description: Visit the plaza and discover opera, dance, orchestral music and other performances in a striking cultural setting.
do: Explore the plaza, enquire about a performance, buy tickets.
why: A more elegant and less predictable evening option.
location: Upper West Side, Broadway at 65th Street; subway 1 to 66 St–Lincoln Center.
